==English==
{{wp}}

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/haɪnd/}}
* {{audio|en|en-us-hind.ogg|a=US}}
* {{rhymes|en|aɪnd|s=1}}

===Etymology 1===
{{etymon|en|id=rear|:inh|enm:hinde<ety:inh<ang:hindan>>|tree=1}}
From {{inh|en|enm|hinde}}, from {{inh|en|ang|hindan|t=at the rear, from behind}}, {{der|en|gem-pro|*hinder||behind, beyond}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*ḱem-ta-||down, below, with, far, along, against}}, from {{m|ine-pro|*ḱóm||beside, near, by, with}}. Cognate with {{cog|got|𐌷𐌹𐌽𐌳𐌰𐌽𐌰||from beyond}}, {{cog|non|hindr||obstacle}}, {{cog|non|handan||from that side, beyond}}, {{cog|goh|hintana||behind}}, {{cog|de|hinter||behind, beyond}}, {{cog|ang|hinder||behind, back, in the farthest part, down}}, {{cog|la|contra||in return, against}}. More at {{l|en|hinder}}, {{l|en|contrary}}.

====Adjective====
{{en-adj|hinder|sup=hindmost}}

# Located at the [[rear]] (most often said of animals' body parts).
#* {{RQ:Burroughs Land That Time Forgot||V|passage=When it had advanced from the wood, it hopped much after the fashion of a kangaroo, using its '''hind''' feet and tail to propel it, and when it stood erect, it sat upon its tail.}}
# [[backward|Backward]]; to the rear.

===Etymology 2===
{{etymon|en|:inh|enm:hynde|id=deer|tree=1}}
{{wikispecies|Epinephelus}}
{{inh+|en|enm|hynde|id=deer}}, {{m|enm|hynd}}, from {{inh|en|ang|hind}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*hindi}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*hindō}}, {{m|gem-pro|*hindiz}}, from a formation on {{der|en|ine-pro|*ḱem-||hornless}}. Cognate with {{cog|nl|hinde}}, {{cog|de|Hinde}}, {{cog|da|hind}}.

====Noun====
{{en-noun|~|*|s}}

# A [[doe]] ([[female]] [[deer]]), especially a [[red deer]] at least two years old.
#* {{RQ:Burton Melancholy|edition=2nd|part=III|section=1|member=3|passage=Nature binds all creatures to love their young ones; an hen to preserve her brood will run upon a lion, an '''hind''' will fight with a bull, a sow with a bear, a silly sheep with a fox.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1769|author={{w|Firishta}}|tlr={{w|Alexander Dow}}|title=Tales translated from the Persian of Inatulla of Delhi|volume=I|publisher=P. and W. Wilson et al.|location=Dublin|page=v|text=The ſpring diſplaying her elegant taſte, the proud walk of the gold-feathered pheaſant, the light tread of the ſmall-hoofed '''hind''', and the dancing of the ſtar-trained peacock, infuſed joy into the ſoul of the ſpectator of the aſtoniſhing works of the Creator.}}
# A spotted [[food fish]] of the [[genus]] {{taxfmt|Epinephelus|genus}}.

===Etymology 3===
{{ety|en|:inh|enm:hyne|id=servant|tree=1}}
{{inh+|en|enm|hyne}}, from {{der|en|ang|hīna}}, genitive of {{m|ang|hīgan|g=p||servants, household}}, in the phrase ''hīna fæder'' ‘paterfamilias’. The ''-d'' is a later addition; it usually expained as a phonetic excrescence like in {{m|en|sound}}.<ref>{{R:en:ODEE|hind<sup>2</sup>|441|1}}</ref> But influence from {{senseno|en|rear|t=rear}} or its relatives (especially the reflexes of {{m+|gem-pro|*hinder}}) is also possible, as has been suggested for the cognate {{cog|ofs|hīnde}}: the low-status servant can be easily conceptualised as an individual who is "behind" in a hierarchical sequence.<ref>{{R:ofs:OFED|-higen|171}}</ref><ref>{{cite-journal|year=1915|last=Heinertz|first=N[ils] Otto|authorlink=sv:N. Otto Heinertz|title=Friesisches. 4. Beiträge zur altfriesischen Wörtkunde|journal=w:Indogermanische Forschungen|volume=35|publisher=[[w:Verlag Karl J. Trübner|Verlag von Karl Trübner]]|location=[[w:Strasbourg|Strassburg]]|doi=10.1515/9783110242751.304
|oclc=6032352901|page=319|pageurl=https://archive.org/details/indogermanischef35berluoft/page/318}}</ref>

====Noun====
{{en-noun}}

# {{lb|en|archaic}} A servant, especially an agricultural [[labourer]].
#* {{RQ:Montaigne Florio Essayes|chapter=Of the Parcimony of Our Forefathers|book=I|page=167|passage=''Attilius Regulus'' {{...}} writ vnto the common-wealth, that a '''hynde''', or plough-boy whom he had left alone to over-ſee and husband his land (which in all was but ſeaven acres of ground) was run away from his charge{{nb...}}.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|author=Robert Bowmaker|chapter=Number LI. Parish of Dunse, (County of Berwick.)|editor=[[w:Sir John Sinclair, 1st Baronet|John Sinclair]]|title=[[w:Statistical Accounts of Scotland|The Statistical Account of Scotland. Drawn Up from the Communications of the Ministers of the Different Parishes]]|location=Edinburgh|publisher=Printed and sold by William Creech [''et al.'']|year=1792|volume=IV|page=386|pageurl=https://books.google.com/books?id=e1deAAAAcAAJ&pg=PA386|oclc=499791781|passage=The farmers ſervants who have families, and engage by the year, are called '''hinds''', and receive 10 [[boll]]s oats, 2 bolls barley, and 1 boll peas, which two laſt articles are called hummel corn, {{...}}}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1827|author=Maria Elizabeth Budden|url=http://books.google.co.uk/books?id=GLYNAAAAYAAJ|title=Nina, An Icelandic Tale|page=41
|passage=The peaceful tenour of Nina's life was interrupted one morning by the mysterious looks and whisperings of her maids and '''hinds'''.}}
#* {{RQ:Buck Good Earth|passage=that my brother can sit at leisure in a seat and learn something and I must work like a '''hind''', who am your son as well as he!}}
#* {{see more citations|en}}
